## Purpose
`commands/git_settle.rs`, `commands/maint/claude_dir_prune.rs` and `commands/maint/rehook.rs` are three of the 14 top-level entry modules a `run <subcommand>` dispatches to. Each owns an `Opts` struct for its CLI flags, a `run(opts)`/`dispatch(cmd)` function that is the module's one public entry point, and a heavily-documented module header explaining the invariant it enforces (fail-open contract, what it may/may not act on). This mold teaches the shape a new subcommand's entry file must follow.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 14
All three exemplars open with a long `//!` doc comment naming the exact `mustard-rt run <name>` invocation, its fail-open contract, and (for `git_settle.rs`, `rehook.rs`) a numbered list of the steps/shapes it handles. Each declares a small `pub struct <Name>Opts` (plain fields, no `Default` derive observed) for CLI-supplied options, and JSON/serde report structs (`RestoredEntry`, `RehookReport`) with `#[derive(Serialize)]` and `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on optional fields. Helper functions used only by the entry module stay private (no `pub`) unless a sibling module in the same family needs them, in which case they are `pub(crate)`.

## How to apply
A new `run <subcommand>` lands as its own file under `commands/` or `commands/<family>/`, with an `Opts` struct, a `run`/`dispatch` entry function, and a report type serialized as byte-stable JSON. Register it per the CLAUDE.md four-registration rule: the `{Family}Cmd` enum variant + its `dispatch()` arm in the family's `cli.rs`, the locked list in `tests/run_command_surface.rs`, and a real caller (or a justified `RUNTIME_WHITELIST` entry) in `tests/template_parity.rs`.
